name: v15.10.1
body:
A bug-fix release. No new settings and no breaking changes.

## Reliability

- Context reads keep working when the database's `-wal` and wal-index files are missing. (#5432 by @0xABCD01)
- Queued batches are kept, not dropped, when Claude replies with a 429 rate limit. (#5430 by @markjoin123)
- A stalled session's buffered work is discarded once its resume attempts are used up, so it no longer blocks the queue. (#5414 by @0xABCD01)
- SSE frames queued for a slow consumer are now bounded. (#5395 by @liuyinchu)
- The observer response deadline has its own constant. (#5406 by @lunetics)
- The observer fills missing proxy settings from your Claude user settings. (#5401 by @markjoin123)
- `/api/processing-status` reports sessions the stall pacer abandoned and the observer's last successful store time. (#5409, #5408 by @xunguangzlj-cloud)
- Settings: SessionStart toggles persist, and zero context counts are accepted via `POST /api/settings`. (#5393 by @0xABCD01)

## Security

- All TeamBrain routes reject requests from foreign origins. (#5411 by @DeryFerd)
- Perplexity API keys are redacted. (#5407 by @mertkayacs)

## Viewer and My Work

- My Work sharing stays on for the cloud viewer. (#5433 by @thedotmack)
- Unparseable work-view frames are dropped instead of throwing. (#5412 by @DeryFerd)
- Hosted usage reaches PostHog again (`randomUUID` is called on `crypto`). (#5421 by @thedotmack)
- Windows file paths are shortened on observation cards. (#5419 by @Plastic-time)

## Search and smart-read

- Dumb search keeps fetchable memories ahead of prompts. (#5397 by @liuyinchu)
- Search recalls supplementary Han and extended Katakana characters. (#5396 by @liuyinchu)
- Outlines include C and C++ unions, and Zig struct, enum, union and opaque declarations. (#5403, #5402 by @L4XB)

## Install, CLI and platforms

- The installer writes MCP JSON configs atomically. (#5413 by @DeryFerd)
- Agent-driven installs are guided into the user's browser setup, and the docs list the terminal prompts an agent must relay. (#5379 by @thedotmack)
- Cursor: reads and searches are recorded through Cursor's `postToolUse` hook. (#5399 by @Lumea-art)
- `--help` after a verb shows help instead of running the command. (#5394 by @Bortlesboat)
- Windows: the data directory removal command works, and integration tests stay out of the fast lane. (#5420, #5418 by @Plastic-time)

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/compare/v15.10.0...v15.10.1

name: v15.10.0
body:
## What's new

**Onboarding finds your existing work.** Setup now leads with discovering your existing work, rules and focus from your transcripts. The main button is "Discover My Work, Rules & Focus", and "Skip this step" is a smaller action under it. The "Share anonymous usage statistics to help improve your Claude-mem experience" box starts checked; unchecking it is kept, and nothing is sent until you press Discover. When hosted setup is busy, claude-mem checks capacity before uploading, remembers the cooldown across restarts and lets you finish setup. (#5270, #5308, #5384 by @thedotmack)

**Turn memory capture off.** New `CLAUDE_MEM_OBSERVER_ENABLED` setting and a Memory capture toggle. Set it to `"false"` to stop new observation and summary model calls while keeping existing memories, search and session-start context. (#5353 by @tarunbad)

**Pick the observer per tool.** New `CLAUDE_MEM_PROVIDER_BY_SOURCE` setting picks the observer provider per session source, for example Codex sessions on Codex and Claude Code sessions on Claude. (#5333 by @ankit4479)

**Long-lived Claude login.** `~/.claude-mem/.env` can now supply `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, so capture doesn't stop when the stored Claude Code login expires. Sessions paused for auth resume once a credential is shown to work. (#5372 by @MeggDistribution, #5383 by @xunguangzlj-cloud)

**Combine modes.** Mode overrides now chain, so a language mode can combine with chill, like `code--chill--ko`. (#5349 by @BaeJinSeop)

**Doctor explains a missing observer.** `npx claude-mem doctor` now reports an unavailable observer provider and the worker's dependencies, instead of saying all is well. (#5366 by @parveen0029)

**Viewer sync and My Work.** Viewer sync recovery is now on main: faster bounded views, truthful sync status, shared My Work state between devices, and recovery of remote changes. On the cloud viewer, My Work links to Account & billing. (#5410, #5416 by @thedotmack)

## Reliability

- The worker waits for a free slot instead of failing when the pool of 10 is full, and releases an idle slot when other sessions are waiting. (#5386 by @balabommablock-cpu, #5388 by @0xABCD01)
- Hung context-reader requests now time out, so a stuck read no longer stops observations. (#5387 by @markjoin123)
- Failure tracking restarts when the kind of failure changes. (#5380 by @xunguangzlj-cloud)
- Codex exits are classified only from their recent stderr. (#5310 by @2023Anita)
- The observer no longer inherits a parent gateway's model names, and keeps your Claude beta opt-out. A model refusal is reported as a model outage. (#5316 by @sayedrisat, #5317 by @parveen0029, #5348 by @tarunbad)
- SSE streams keep their framing across chunk boundaries, and the viewer ignores frames it can't parse. (#5367 by @Afloat16, #5364 by @DeryFerd)
- Capped error-body readers release their locks. (#5340 by @Afloat16)
- Bug reports fall back to the template when the SDK doesn't finish a report. (#5302 by @liuyinchu)

## Install and platforms

- Windows: the worker daemon starts without PowerShell. (#5351 by @REI-330)
- Copilot CLI: the MCP server is registered in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, where Copilot CLI reads it. (#5305 by @tanishqbaweja)
- Goose on Windows: claude-mem is registered in `%APPDATA%\Block\goose\config`. (#5323 by @tanishqbaweja)
- Devin: context is injected again after Devin compacts a session. (#5314 by @patrickballard)
- Kimi: hook commands stay valid TOML when a path contains a quote. (#5363 by @DeryFerd)
- Docker: the server and worker share the same BullMQ queue prefix, and the docs list tested Redis-compatible servers. The sync-api container runs as a non-root user. (#5389, #5390 by @murtazayusuf, #5331 by @DeryFerd)
- Process identity probes are pinned to UTC. (#5312 by @LuckVd)

## Import and search

- Prompt import reads the Codex and OpenCode profiles set by `CODEX_HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME`, includes committed OpenCode WAL updates, recognizes OpenCode tool inputs as agent-authored, excludes copied Codex fork prompts, decodes JSON tool strings, and keeps hook prompts when session reads are incomplete. (#5303, #5297, #5304, #5300, #5369, #5301 by @rudycelekli)
- Adoption keeps the real checkout paths before remapping memories, and checkout identity keeps whitespace. (#5296 by @rudycelekli, #5368 by @liuyinchu)
- Folder searches match relative backslash paths and extensionless files like `Makefile`. (#5309 by @rudycelekli, #5343 by @liuyinchu)
- Chroma's semantic fallback query no longer includes `doc_type`. (#5355 by @0xABCD01)
- Compact times handle the U+202F separator before AM/PM. (#5356 by @kevin9327)

## Privacy and security

- More secrets are redacted before they are stored: Groq, xAI, NVIDIA NIM, Runcrate, Google OAuth (`ya29.`), Linear, Notion, Supabase, Sentry, Databricks and HashiCorp Vault tokens. (#5298, #5342, #5345, #5352, #5373 by @kevin9327; #5327 by @DeryFerd)
- Log values with line breaks are escaped so they can't forge a log record. (#5328 by @DeryFerd)
- Sync: a 402 verify response drops the cached verdict, the per-isolate auth memo is bounded, and advisory sockets close when their auth verdict lapses. (#5329, #5332 by @DeryFerd; #5358 by @REI-330)
- Input bounds on batch id arrays, timeline depth, the job listing offset and empty URL modifiers; numeric-string ids are accepted in `/api/observations/batch`. (#5360, #5362, #5361, #5330 by @DeryFerd; #5341 by @Afloat16; #5336 by @ryrenz)
- Hermes strips memory tags with a linear scan. (#5320 by @REI-330)

## Docs

- Development prerequisites and test instructions match current tooling; the README lists every built-in language mode; Simplified Chinese and Vietnamese READMEs are synced. (#5324 by @POWDER-RANGER, #5334 by @BaeJinSeop, #5322 by @h6rime, #5391 by @vietmy1711)
- Test fix for macOS SQLite. (#5313 by @patrickballard)

Thank you to everyone who contributed to this release.

name: supervision-0.31.5
body:
# v0.31.5: Line counts through occlusion, the exact clipper for oriented boxes, and right-to-left labels

Right-to-left labels, line counting that survives occlusion, and a batch of edge-case fixes across annotators, exports and the NumPy fallback.

- **LineZone** counts objects that are hidden for a few frames while they cross the line.
- Arabic and Hebrew labels render correctly with the new `rtl` extra.
- Oriented-box IoU, NMS and metrics now use the exact clipper on OpenCV installs.
- Annotating a Pillow image keeps its transparency and untouched pixels.
- Heat maps and ellipse halos now work on grayscale scenes.

It's a drop-in upgrade, but check the Migration guide if you count line crossings, score-oriented boxes on OpenCV, or compare stored outputs.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### Right-to-left labels with the new `rtl` extra

`sv.RichLabelAnnotator` now draws Arabic and Hebrew labels correctly on RGB and RGBA images when the new `rtl` extra is installed. Pillow only joins Arabic letters and orders right-to-left text when it's built with Raqm, and most Windows installs and many containers lack it. There, `"سيارة 0.92"` came out as isolated letters in reverse order. Lines with Arabic or Hebrew are now shaped in the label's font, using fallback Arabic and Hebrew fonts from `khatt` for missing glyphs, and right-aligned in the background box. Other image modes fall back to Pillow, with a warning that suggests RGB or RGBA when Raqm is missing. Without the extra, a one-time warning names it. (#2864)

```python
# pip install "supervision[rtl]"
import supervision as sv

label_annotator = sv.RichLabelAnnotator(font_path="NotoNaskhArabic-Regular.ttf")
annotated = label_annotator.annotate(
    scene=image, detections=detections, labels=["سيارة 0.92"]
)
```

### `LineZone` counts objects occluded while crossing

If a tracker disappears for a few frames while crossing the line, it's still counted. By default, `sv.LineZone` drops a tracker's stored side after `max(30, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)` consecutive absent frames. It used to drop it after `max(2, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)`, which is 2 at the default threshold. The new `max_absent_frames` parameter sets this. Counts can rise against 0.31.4 on the same input. (#2873)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

line = sv.LineZone(start=sv.Point(0, 50), end=sv.Point(100, 50))


def detection(y):
    return sv.Detections(
        xyxy=np.array([[40.0, y - 10, 60.0, y]]), tracker_id=np.array([1])
    )


line.trigger(detection(40))  # above the line
for _ in range(5):  # occluded for five frames
    line.trigger(sv.Detections.empty())
line.trigger(detection(80))  # reappears below the line
line.in_count, line.out_count
# (0, 1)  (0.31.4: (0, 0))

# Restore the old retention:
sv.LineZone(start=sv.Point(0, 50), end=sv.Point(100, 50), max_absent_frames=2)
```

### The exact clipper for oriented boxes on OpenCV installs

`sv.oriented_box_iou_batch`, OBB NMS and OBB metrics now use the same convex clipper on OpenCV installs that the NumPy fallback uses. With OpenCV, rotated boxes with nearly collinear overlapping edges, and boxes with both sides far below one coordinate unit, could get an IoU of 0 or 1. The clipper is roughly 10x slower per candidate pair than the OpenCV call, so crowded scenes can take seconds. Oriented-box precision, recall, F1, and mean average recall also keep corner precision at large coordinate origins. (#2882, #2887)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv


def rotated(width, height, degrees, center=(200.0, 200.0)):
    t = np.deg2rad(degrees)
    u = np.array([np.cos(t), np.sin(t)]) * width / 2
    v = np.array([-np.sin(t), np.cos(t)]) * height / 2
    c = np.array(center)
    return np.array([[c - u - v, c + u - v, c + u + v, c - u + v]])


t = np.deg2rad(10)
a = rotated(100, 40, 10)
b = a + np.array([np.cos(t), np.sin(t)]) * 50  # true IoU is 0.3333
sv.oriented_box_iou_batch(a, b)[0, 0]
# 0.3333  (0.31.4 with OpenCV: 1.0)
```

### Pillow scenes keep the pixels annotators do not draw

Annotators handed a `PIL.Image` now change only the pixels they draw. A transparent RGBA or LA background stays transparent, and a 16-bit (`I;16`) or 32-bit (`I`) image keeps the depth of its untouched pixels, with drawn pixels scaled back to the 16-bit range. Before, the whole image went through an 8-bit round trip. (#2883)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from PIL import Image

scene = Image.new("RGBA", (100, 100), (0, 0, 0, 0))
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[20.0, 20.0, 60.0, 60.0]]), class_id=np.array([0])
)
annotated = sv.BoxAnnotator().annotate(scene, detections)
annotated.getpixel((0, 0))
# (0, 0, 0, 0)  (0.31.4: (0, 0, 0, 255))
```

## 🔄 Migration guide

No public symbol was removed or renamed, and nothing is deprecated. A few fixes change what existing code returns or draws:

- **Different counts:** `LineZone` keeps a tracker's side for `max(30, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)` absent frames instead of 2, so `in_count` and `out_count` can rise on the same input. Pass `max_absent_frames=max(2, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)` to restore the old retention. (#2873)
- **Different scores and speed on OpenCV installs:** oriented-box IoU, NMS and metrics use the exact clipper, roughly 10x slower per candidate pair. Regenerate any stored IoU, NMS and mAP references. (#2882, #2887)
- **Different pixels and files:** Pillow scenes keep unannotated pixels (#2883), `as_coco` writes mask holes joined to their outline (#2879), and the GHUM skeleton gains its left wrist-to-left-index edge (#2876).
- **New error without OpenCV:** the `cvtColor` fallback reads float32 `COLOR_HSV2BGR` input as OpenCV does (hue in degrees, other values in `[0, 1]`) and raises `ValueError` for depths OpenCV rejects. Convert float32 HSV to that scale, or cast to `uint8`, first. (#2885)
- **Video reads:** `get_video_frames_generator` stops at the requested end instead of reading excluded frames. (#2874)

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🚀 Added

- **`rtl` extra.** `pip install "supervision[rtl]"` installs `khatt`, and `RichLabelAnnotator` then shapes Arabic and Hebrew lines in the label font, with fallback fonts from `khatt` for missing glyphs. Without the extra and without Raqm, a one-time warning names it. (#2864)
- **`LineZone(max_absent_frames=...)`.** Sets how many consecutive missing frames pass before a tracker's crossing state is dropped; values below 1 raise `ValueError`. (#2873)

### 🌱 Changed

- `LineZone` default retention goes from `max(2, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)` to `max(30, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)` absent frames, so occluded objects are counted. (#2873)
- `oriented_box_iou_batch`, OBB NMS and OBB metrics use the convex clipper of the NumPy fallback on OpenCV installs, so IoU can differ for affected pairs; expect roughly 10x the cost per candidate pair. (#2882)

### 🔧 Fixed

**Annotators**

- Annotators given a `PIL.Image` change only the pixels they draw: RGBA and LA transparency stays, and `I;16` and `I` images keep the depth of untouched pixels. (#2883)
- `HeatMapAnnotator` and `VertexEllipseHaloAnnotator` annotate grayscale scenes, shaped `(H, W)`, `(H, W, 1)` or a Pillow `"L"` image, instead of raising `ValueError`. (#2872, #2878)

**Detections, zones and metrics**

- `oriented_box_iou_batch` on OpenCV installs no longer reports an IoU of 0 or 1 for rotated boxes with nearly collinear overlapping edges, or for boxes with both sides far below one coordinate unit. (#2882)
- Oriented-box precision, recall, F1 and mean average recall keep corner precision at large coordinate origins, so perfect predictions there are no longer misses or filed under the wrong object-size category. (#2887)
- `np.sum` works on a `CompactMask`, with or without `axis`, and matches the dense mask for `dtype`, `out`, `keepdims`, `initial` and `where`; it raised `TypeError` before. (#2880)
- `Detections.get_anchors_coordinates(Position.CENTER_OF_MASS)` returns an empty `(0, 2)` array for an empty batch without masks instead of raising `ValueError`; a populated batch without masks still raises. (#2877)
- `CSVSink` keeps an exception raised inside a `with` block when cleanup also raises; the cleanup exception is logged. (#2869)

**Datasets and exports**

- `as_coco` keeps the holes of masks written as polygons with `iscrowd=0`, joining them to the outline instead of writing extra polygon parts that readers fill in; a hole that cannot be joined warns and keeps the old parts. (#2879)
- Hole bridging in `as_yolo`, `as_pascal_voc` and `as_labelme` retries top-down, so valid masks with an enclosed hole listed before its outer hole no longer raise `ValueError`. (#2879)
- COCO export computes box width, height and area with Python scalars: without a mask or stored area, a `300×300` `float16` or `int16` box exports an area of `90000` instead of infinity or `24464`. (#2867)

**Key points, video and windows**

- `Skeleton.GHUM` (in `supervision.key_points.skeletons`) connects the left wrist to the left index finger; `EdgeAnnotator` had drawn a bone from the right elbow to the right pinky on 33-keypoint poses. (#2876)
- `get_video_frames_generator` stops reading and skipping at the requested end. (#2874)
- `ImageWindow.show` draws the frame on the call that opens the window, opens at the frame's size up to the screen size without growing on each redraw, and fits frames with a one-pixel dimension. (#2881)

**NumPy fallback without OpenCV**

- `cvtColor` accepts BGRA input for `COLOR_BGR2GRAY` and `(H, W, 1)` input for `COLOR_GRAY2BGR`, so `grayscale_image` no longer fails on BGRA frames. (#2866)
- `blur` on `uint16` and `int16` images uses exact integer window sums and OpenCV's scaling precision. (#2875)
- `cvtColor` reads float32 `COLOR_HSV2BGR` input as OpenCV does. (#2885)

## 🏆 Contributors

Welcome to our first-time contributors, Mohammad Essam, Barsam Ershadi, and oha!

- **Barsam Ershadi** (@BarsamErshadi, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/barsam-ershadi/)) – grayscale heat maps and halos, COCO mask holes, `np.sum` on `CompactMask`, empty-batch center-of-mass anchors, window fixes, the GHUM wrist edge and the oriented-box overlap clipper.
- **kevin** (@kevin9327) – made the `cvtColor` and `blur` fallbacks follow OpenCV for BGRA, gray, 16-bit and float32 input.
- **Mohammad Essam** (@DrEssam97, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohammad-essam97)) – shaped Arabic and Hebrew labels in `RichLabelAnnotator` with the `rtl` extra.
- **NIKHIL** (@Nikhi00718, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nikhil-v-engineer)) – made `LineZone` count objects occluded while they cross.
- **A Aswanth Raj** (@aswanth-07, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/a-aswanth-raj/)) – kept oriented-box metric precision at large coordinate origins.
- **LEE, WEI-HONG** (@AuricTW) – fixed COCO area overflow and kept `with` block exceptions in `CSVSink`.
- **Mohammad Hijjawi** (@MohammadHijjawi97, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohammadhijjawi)) – kept unannotated pixels of Pillow scenes unchanged.
- **Devulapalli Naga Sri Vaishnavi** (@Vaishnavi220506, [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/vaishnavi-d-9a42a9374)) – stopped the video frame generator at the requested end.
- **oha** (@duriantaco) – removed unused code.
- **Jirka Borovec** (@Borda, [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/jirka-borovec)) – prepared the release.

*Automated contributions: pre-commit.ci*

name: graphify 0.9.103
body:
## graphify 0.9.103

A broad correctness, performance and robustness release across the extractors, resolution, hooks, the query and update paths, install and the skill runbook.

### Extractors
- **C#**: preprocessor directives and `#if` branches that derail tree-sitter are blanked before parsing (byte-length preserving), so a directive no longer closes a class early and drops later members or calls.
- **Solidity**: library calls (`Lib.f()`, including aliased imports) and `emit`/`revert`/`require` naming a declared event or error now link to the member they name, gated to a unique visible type and member.
- **YAML**: a `<<` merge sequence gives the earlier anchor precedence for a duplicated key, matching the spec and PyYAML.
- **Markdown**: a code span written as a backslash namespace (`\Foo\Bar`) or a type-qualified member (`Type::member`) resolves to the real node; a dotted mention whose method name is a language builtin is no longer dropped.
- **Python**: a bare builtin-named call (`raise NotImplementedError(...)`) no longer binds to a same-named class in another module unless imported.

### Resolution
- A call inside a top-level `def _main()` is attributed to `_main`, not the public `main` it collides with after id normalization, without misattributing a class member's type reference.

### Hooks
- A file unchanged in content is not re-flagged stale by mtime (the extraction hash is checked against the manifest).
- A dedicated Grep is held to the strict orientation gate; a Bash file read (`cat`/`head`/`sed -n`) of an in-project code file gets the read nudge; a search whose every target is outside the project emits no project hint; the nudge budget is restored after a Claude Code compaction; and the toplevel anchor keeps working when `CDPATH` is exported.

### Performance
- Lower peak memory in load, resolution and extraction; a faster `#3252` cross-file repoint; and the watch reconcile pass resolves AST ownership once per file instead of re-reading each header per node — all with identical graph output.

### Update / build / cache
- `graphify update` re-extracts only the files whose content changed (identical to a full rebuild); a contended incremental request is recorded instead of dropped. The build write guard no longer counts intentional ghost/dedup folds as drops; cache keys keep their written case.

### Query / tree
- Source nodes rank above tests and docs (a soft weight) with file-first answers; `query` reads `query_budget`/`query_depth` from `.graphifyrc` and gains `--depth`. `export tree` caps directory children while reporting full totals.

### Install / thread-safety
- The Pi project skill is written to `.pi/skills`; uninstall removes the global skill registration it wrote. The ambient scan root is held in a `ContextVar` so concurrent library callers extracting different roots do not clobber each other.

The AST cache schema is bumped to 39; warm caches re-run the affected extractions.

Thanks to @rohit-jsfreaky, @Deepjyoti-Sarmah, @xiongjianxu, @nothariharan, @andrebrait, @ajbmachon, @Shubham-Padkonde, @madhusudanpatnaik, @pei711, @Mpasha17, @ayushcodes10, @gitmotion, @briascoi, @oleksii-tumanov, @rohit-jsfreaky, @viwe-monai, @WyattAu, @Vivek1898, @wanjinhao1, @PratikDhanave, @HhH666-ux, @sunhouy, @mathewgeejo, @jinsoo and @AndresDiagoM.

name: v1.65.0
body:
## 🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under [Bun](https://bun.com). Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the `--bun` flag, because without it `bunx playwright test` runs on Node.js:

```bash
bunx --bun playwright test
```

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

- There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and `--only-changed` does not follow imports.
- Bun loads modules itself, so `--tsconfig` and the JSX options in `tsconfig.json` have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
- Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: `click` instead of `locator.click`. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
- Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

## 🚨 Reports with only failures

New [`failures`](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-reporters#failures-reporter) reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New `onlyFailures` option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters [keeps only](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-reporters#report-only-failures) tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

```js
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  reporter: [
    ['failures'],
    ['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
  ],
});
```

## 🎯 Test runner

- New built-in `-exclusive-` [test lock](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-parallel#test-locks) runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

  ```js
  test('restart the server', { lock: '-exclusive-' }, async () => {
    // No other test runs while this one is running.
  });
  ```

- [test.skip()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-skip), [test.fixme()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-fixme), [test.fail()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-fail) and [test.slow()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-slow) now accept only a description. It is recorded in the test annotation:

  ```js
  test('upload a file', async ({ page }) => {
    test.skip('Not implemented yet');
  });
  ```

- New `PLAYWRIGHT_TRANSFORM_CACHE_DIR` environment variable sets the directory for transpiled test files, for example on a Linux machine shared with other users.

## New APIs

- New options [`timeout`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-cdpsession#cdp-session-send-option-timeout) and [`signal`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-cdpsession#cdp-session-send-option-signal) in [cdpSession.send()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-cdpsession#cdp-session-send).
- New [testRun.mode()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testrun#test-run-mode) returns the execution mode of a suite during [reporter.preprocess()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-reporter#reporter-preprocess).

## Breaking Changes ⚠️

- TypeScript class fields now follow [`useDefineForClassFields`](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-typescript#tsconfig-class-fields) from your `tsconfig.json`, the same as `tsc`. It is enabled for `ES2022` and later targets, and when `target` is not specified. A field initializer that reads a constructor parameter property now fails, because the initializer runs first:

  ```js
  class LoginPage {
    // TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getByRole')
    readonly submit = this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });

    constructor(private readonly page: Page) {}
  }
  ```

  Move the initialization to the constructor, or set `"useDefineForClassFields": false` in your `tsconfig.json`.

- Actions such as [locator.click()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-click), [locator.check()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-check), [locator.tap()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-tap), [locator.fill()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-fill), [locator.clear()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-clear) and [locator.selectOption()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-select-option) now wait for the element to be [not inert](https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability#not-inert). An action on an element with the `inert` attribute, or inside such an element, now times out if the element stays inert.

- A sharded run now fails with "No tests found" when no tests match across all shards. Pass `--pass-with-no-tests` to allow this. An empty shard still passes when other shards have tests.

- Cookie matching now follows RFC 6265. With a URL, [browserContext.cookies()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-cookies) and [apiRequestContext.cookies()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-apirequestcontext#api-request-context-cookies) no longer return host-only cookies for subdomains or `Path=/api` cookies for `/apiv2`, and a `Path=/foo/` cookie does not match `/foo`. [APIRequestContext](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-apirequestcontext) sends a cookie without a name as `Cookie: x` instead of `Cookie: =x`, and stores `Set-Cookie: token` as a cookie without a name.

- Proxy credentials are no longer sent to websites. The credentials in the [`proxy`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-launch-option-proxy) option now answer only proxy challenges. To authenticate on a website, use [`httpCredentials`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context-option-http-credentials).

- Text that the browser does not render, such as text that is not assigned to a slot or text directly inside a closed `<details>`, is no longer part of accessible names and aria snapshots. This can change the results of [page.getByRole()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-role) with a name, [locator.ariaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-aria-snapshot) and [expect(locator).toMatchAriaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locatorassertions#locator-assertions-to-match-aria-snapshot).

- String and `URLSearchParams` values of the `params` option in [APIRequestContext](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-apirequestcontext) requests are now appended to the query that the URL already has, instead of replacing it.

- `.css`, `.less` and `.scss` imports in test files now load as empty modules instead of being removed, so the imported file must exist.

- The blob reporter again deletes the content of its output directory before it writes the report. Playwright 1.64 kept reports with other names.

- Test locations of imported calls such as `test(` in CommonJS output now point to the start of the callee, for example `a.spec.ts:3:7` instead of `a.spec.ts:3:11`. This is the same as in ESM.

## Announcements

* ⚠️ Playwright no longer tests on Node.js 20. Use Node.js 22, 24 or 26, as listed in the [system requirements](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro#system-requirements).
* 🐳 [Docker images](https://playwright.dev/docs/docker) now include Node.js 26 instead of Node.js 24, and the latest patch of Chromium on the same branch.

## Browser Versions

- Chromium 158.0.8127.18
- Mozilla Firefox 159.0
- WebKit 27.2

This version was also tested against the following stable channels:

- Google Chrome 157
- Microsoft Edge 156

## [3.0.0-alpha.5] ### Breaking Changes - [`78f49ba39`](https://www.github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/commit/78f49ba3993fed5a1b921235c547731006ad2a74) ([#16077](https://www.github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/pull/16077) by [@amrbashir](https://www.github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/../../amrbashir)) Removed `WindowDispatch::on_window_event` and `WebviewDispatch::on_webview_event`, along with the `WindowEventId` and `WebviewEventId` types. Runtimes already report every window and webview event through `RunEvent::WindowEvent` / `RunEvent::WebviewEvent`, so the per-window listener registries each runtime kept were a duplicate of that stream. **Migration:** custom runtimes should drop their `on_window_event`/`on_webview_event` implementations and their listener storage; emitting `RunEvent::WindowEvent` and `RunEvent::WebviewEvent` is now the only thing required to deliver events.

name: v2.1.4
body:
### Security
- Deny rules now apply to every shell language of ctx_execute (sh, bash, zsh, dash, ksh, fish) and to ctx_batch commands, checked per command segment like the Bash tool. The deny check now runs in linear time, so long input stays inside the hook budget. ([bcd2921](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/commit/bcd29213273617ab639741596d04b77544026df1))
- Fetch blocks more private and special address ranges (shared 100.64.0.0/10, 0.0.0.0/8, 198.18.0.0/15, 240.0.0.0/4, fec0::/10, ::/96, 64:ff9b:1::/48), checks the IPv4 address inside NAT64 and 6to4 addresses, and checks every redirect hop. Stored line units now grow linearly with input size. ([6de3349](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/commit/6de334950b312db039dd51f783fc8dd23f542677))
- ctx_upgrade keeps v1 data: old v1 data dirs are moved aside and kept, and a path reached through a link is reported and left as is. The PostToolUse hook reads persisted output only from its own session dir, as a plain file of at most 16 MiB. ([54c4e2d](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/commit/54c4e2d0455dcdd6b184e8d925b9741388d2ebb8))

### Fixes
- fix: guard test keeps the Claude Code Agent input unchanged on first call and resend (#1319)
- fix: setup writes the stable Homebrew node link, so brew upgrade node keeps hooks and MCP running
- fix: ctx_upgrade keeps v1 data and never follows a project link; hook reads persisted output only from its own session dir
- fix: VS Code server reads the workspace from MCP roots, setup writes no ${workspaceFolder} in the user mcp.json
- fix: ZCode native plugin install, Qwen project scope and Windows hook command, hook overhead as warning
- fix: ctx_upgrade uses each agent's own update command, no release-branch clone (#1309)
- fix: block more private fetch targets and bound line unit size
- fix: OpenCode 2 host (Bun): doctor hook run, background launcher, read-only DB open, D3 entries, read size guard (#1310)
- fix: CONTEXT_MODE_DATA_DIR moves the data root, so each Claude Code profile can keep its own store (#1318)
- fix: gemini native install, GEMINI_CLI_HOME, AfterTool replace wording, Part lists
- fix: apply user deny rules to every shell ctx_execute language, per segment, in linear time

### Who gets this

One version on both channels: the release commit on main (GitHub) and npm.

| Claude Code | GitHub | `claude plugin update context-mode@context-mode` |

| Qwen Code | GitHub | `qwen extensions update context-mode` |
| Copilot CLI | npm | `context-mode upgrade` |

| ZCode | GitHub | `zcode plugins update context-mode@context-mode` |

name: lume: v0.7.0
body:
# Lume 0.7.0

## Summary

This release adds 4 features and includes 10 fixes.

## Features

- add `lume cp` for host↔guest file transfer. ([#4896](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4896))
- compat gateways for E2B and Daytona, Hetzner as your own cloud, the elastic pool, cua share and the public relay. ([#5778](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5778))
- install source builds as lume-local, beside the released lume. ([#5804](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5804))
- ask first, CI runners, TCP shares, secure networks and the phone app, behind experiments. ([#6355](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6355))

## Fixes

- stop a VM in lume serve without ending the server. ([#4662](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4662))
- preserve legacy multipart disk bytes during assembly. ([#4714](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4714)) Thanks @cooleryu.
- preserve background service during updates. ([#4337](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4337)) Thanks @Iflaqbhat.
- shell-escape remote command arguments in lume ssh (#3879). ([#3911](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3911)) Thanks @shobhitagnihotri69; reported by @jmgilman.
- refuse a macOS guest start at the host's macOS guest limit. ([#3958](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3958)) Thanks @lorenzozanee; reported by @jmgilman.
- report a VM stopped once its guest stops on its own. ([#4853](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4853)) reported by @coygeek.
- pull parameterized OCI tar disk parts. ([#5192](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5192)) Thanks @cooleryu; reported by @zpv.
- print VM details as labeled fields in terminals. ([#5358](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5358)) Thanks @0xABAN.
- verify VM owner before stopping. ([#5611](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5611))
- reach macOS VMs over vsock, not Local Network or VPN routes (CUA-3139). ([#6380](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6380))

## Contributors

Thanks to @0xABAN, @cooleryu, @coygeek, @Iflaqbhat, @jmgilman, @lorenzozanee, @shobhitagnihotri69, @zpv for contributing to this release.

## Install

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/lume/install.sh)"
```

Lume releases include a notarized macOS command-line archive and installer
package, plus stable alias filenames for the install script.

# Cua Spaces 0.21.0

## Summary

This release adds 10 features and includes 2 fixes.

## Features

- ask first, CI runners, TCP shares, secure networks and the phone app, behind experiments. ([#6355](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6355))
- warm pools, a prepared Linux Space and agent harnesses ready in about one second (behind the warm-pools experiment). ([#6472](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6472))
- pick up where you left off in the first run (CUA-3319). ([#6463](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6463))
- the new prompt box with a model and an optional repo. ([#6490](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6490))
- Cua Driver built into Cua Spaces (CUA-2771, CUA-2775). ([#6505](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6505))
- Spaces as a tree and a default Space, behind Labs, with the SDK bindings and CLI (CUA-3413). ([#6508](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6508))
- the warming home stays out of the top bar and off the phone until a person writes into it. ([#6513](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6513))
- Stable / Nightly update channel; betas move to Nightly (CUA-3503). ([#6548](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6548))
- permissions step in the new first run, one permission flow with the Cua Driver page (CUA-3550). ([#6579](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6579))
- Network picker with an "Also allow" list (localhost and local network are siblings). ([#6610](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6610))

## Fixes

- the macOS release build installs Go for the network gateway. ([#6422](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6422))
- Cua Driver runs after the new first run, whatever the Mac shares (CUA-3485). ([#6534](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6534))

# Cua Driver 0.38.1-nightly.20261105.41967274244 (nightly)

Automated immutable nightly built from an exact `main` commit. Nightlies are
opt-in, may be less stable than regular releases, and never replace stable
update discovery.

## Source

- Commit: [`b5125d2eaf2463b7bbac219b19fd281420213e1a`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/commit/b5125d2eaf2463b7bbac219b19fd281420213e1a)
- Changes: [nightly-cua-driver-rs-v0.38.1-nightly.20261104.41772590265…`b5125d2eaf24`](https://github.com/trycua/cua/compare/nightly-cua-driver-rs-v0.38.1-nightly.20261104.41772590265...b5125d2eaf2463b7bbac219b19fd281420213e1a)

## Changes

- **Fix:** tell picom's damage lag from a torn frame in the X11 overlay test. ([#6431](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6431))
- **Feat:** capture embedded startup diagnostics. ([#3281](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3281))
- **Fix:** report a sent but unanswered AT-SPI option pick as may-have-landed. ([#6445](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6445))
- **Fix:** time the batch pause test on a paused clock. ([#6453](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6453))
- **Fix:** treat a niri focus read-back the deadline cut off as unconfirmed. ([#6436](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6436))
- **Fix:** stamp the window-local point on macOS 27 background clicks. ([#5492](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5492)) Thanks @cristicretu.
- **Fix:** stop the Node runtime leaking a libuv handle per future poll. ([#5691](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5691)) Thanks @jhugman, @smraikai.
- **Fix:** keep browser attestation off the renderer while a dialog is open. ([#5524](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5524)) Thanks @abonneth.
- **Fix:** index disabled macOS controls and report enabled: false. ([#5635](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5635)) Thanks @kurtguenther; reported by @will-bogusz.
- **Fix:** remove stale screenshot tool references. ([#2317](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2317))
- **Fix:** return from a dom_event click when its handler opens a dialog. ([#5621](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5621)) Thanks @sahiljagtap08.
- **Fix:** clear clippy -D warnings on main. ([#6461](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6461))
- **Fix:** bind every sdk test socket under a short /tmp dir. ([#6466](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6466))
- **Docs:** run the macOS Lume lane from the verify skill. ([#6476](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6476))
- **Fix:** force embedded mode in the SDK in-process loader tests. ([#6485](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6485))
- **Fix:** normalize list_windows z-index parity. ([#2172](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2172))
- **Fix:** detect Hyprland input internals instead of pinning 0.56.2. ([#6495](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6495)) Thanks @chrisohearn.
- **Fix:** refuse with 'did not verify' when cosign cannot start in install.ps1. ([#6483](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6483)) Thanks @sly321-pixel.

## Contributors

Thanks to @abonneth, @chrisohearn, @cristicretu, @jhugman, @kurtguenther, @sahiljagtap08, @sly321-pixel, @smraikai, @will-bogusz for contributing to or reporting changes in this nightly.

## Exact installation

```bash
CUA_DRIVER_RS_VERSION=nightly-cua-driver-rs-v0.38.1-nightly.20261105.41967274244 /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"
```

body:
# Cua Driver 0.39.0

## Summary

This release adds 9 features and includes 67 fixes.

## Features

- compat gateways for E2B and Daytona, Hetzner as your own cloud, the elastic pool, cua share and the public relay. ([#5778](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5778))
- let macOS actions skip the post-action window-change wait. ([#6033](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6033)) Thanks @gakonst.
- add JPEG screenshots to get_window_state and encode from raw pixels. ([#6042](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6042)) Thanks @gakonst.
- plain, upright agent cursor by default; effects and marks opt-in. ([#6142](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6142))
- add a niri compositor adapter for Linux Wayland. ([#6209](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6209)) Thanks @ayagmar, @injaneity.
- cursor floats while moving, soft halo, lean/heading rotation modes. ([#6325](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6325))
- fast path with act-time target guards, behind a default-off flag (CUA-3102). ([#6332](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6332))
- opt-in refusal of ungranted macOS Automation scripting. ([#5777](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5777)) reported by @nick-inkeep.
- capture embedded startup diagnostics. ([#3281](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/3281))

## Fixes

- keys for a popup an MPX click opened go through the master keyboard of the session that clicked. ([#5652](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5652)) Thanks @CMGS.
- the macOS WindowServer health check treats any app-bundle host as bundled. ([#5680](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5680))
- guard Space-free background window enumeration. ([#5712](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5712)) Thanks @CMGS.
- stabilize the known flaky release-gate tests. ([#5538](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5538))
- build client-kind SDK constructors without rebuilding the driver. ([#5896](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5896))
- give the DOM-click baseline readback a longer budget. ([#5918](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5918))
- remove zero-caller macOS drag and AXValue helpers. ([#5962](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5962))
- remove zero-caller input, portal screencast, sway and overlay functions. ([#5958](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5958))
- inline identical refusal forwarders. ([#5963](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5963))
- delete zero-caller API in cua-driver-core and cua-driver. ([#5815](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5815))
- refuse Windows Chromium clicks from a minimized-window snapshot. ([#5686](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5686)) Thanks @philipljh.
- treat Windows elements read while minimized as stale on resolver-routed clicks. ([#6049](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6049))
- remove dead macOS active-Space helper and single-use snapshot wrapper. ([#6094](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6094))
- drop the unused test-only capture registry action API. ([#6114](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6114))
- share overlay query reads across Linux and Windows. ([#6117](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6117))
- locate Finder by name on macOS. ([#5390](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5390)) Thanks @abonneth.
- map Wayland punctuation shortcut keys. ([#4811](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4811)) Thanks @louistiti.
- restore Windows cursor after foreground window clicks. ([#5772](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5772)) Thanks @BhaveshY.
- honor modifiers during Windows drags. ([#5667](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5667)) Thanks @stanley50z.
- await synthetic smooth-scroll readback. ([#4602](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/4602)) Thanks @Iflaqbhat.
- share the keyring history key provider in cua-driver-core. ([#5895](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5895)) Thanks @injaneity.
- resolve Windows press_key characters on the target's layout. ([#6201](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6201)) Thanks @injaneity; reported by @MankhongGarden.
- deliver libei pointer input to secondary monitors. ([#5853](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5853)) Thanks @injaneity; reported by @Faraclas.
- report denied Linux portal screenshots instead of falling back to X11. ([#6124](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6124))
- share the DevTools /json/version probe across browser adapters. ([#6098](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6098))
- report the current frontmost app on macOS without the overlay. ([#6182](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6182)) Thanks @injaneity; reported by @lucasfdale.
- name current snapshots on a token-only refusal, and refuse a bare row a re-read orphaned. ([#6259](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6259))
- stop the Linux focus restore when the saved window is gone. ([#5596](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5596)) Thanks @CMGS, @injaneity.
- count only the returned elements in an elements diff read. ([#5649](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5649)) Thanks @skap3214.
- never borrow keycode 8 for a Linux text character. ([#5595](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5595)) Thanks @CMGS.
- a file write on the Cua Volume mount no longer fails after the file is in place. ([#6322](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6322)) reported by @stanley50z, @ymqy.
- draw the GNOME helper cursor's tip on the click point. ([#6344](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6344))
- stop the X11 agent cursor splitting in two while it moves. ([#6343](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6343))
- quarantine the linux-kvm concurrent flake, fix the TCC seed lock and the Windows portmap pick. ([#6365](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6365))
- restore the X11 active window by bouncing the core focus when only the WM's record moved. ([#5651](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5651)) Thanks @CMGS.
- record KDE Wayland desktops through the portal ScreenCast. ([#6361](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6361)) Thanks @factory-ain3sh.
- scope bounded launch_app to resources.apps launch grants. ([#5690](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5690)) Thanks @Katechnology; reported by @ShadyElsharnoby.
- paint the macOS cursor overlay as a region, not a full-screen frame. ([#5650](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5650)) Thanks @CMGS.
- expose legacy macOS page fallback. ([#5590](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5590))
- collapse daemon-proxy spawn and test the macOS proxy path. ([#5812](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5812))
- stop unit tests mutating the process environment. ([#6417](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6417))
- keep browser refusal codes through protected scope attestation. ([#5573](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5573)) Thanks @abonneth.
- list bound tabs in the order the browser reports them. ([#5527](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5527)) Thanks @abonneth.
- tell picom's damage lag from a torn frame in the X11 overlay test. ([#6431](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6431))
- report a sent but unanswered AT-SPI option pick as may-have-landed. ([#6445](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6445))
- time the batch pause test on a paused clock. ([#6453](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6453))
- treat a niri focus read-back the deadline cut off as unconfirmed. ([#6436](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6436))
- stamp the window-local point on macOS 27 background clicks. ([#5492](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5492)) Thanks @cristicretu.
- stop the Node runtime leaking a libuv handle per future poll. ([#5691](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5691)) Thanks @jhugman, @smraikai.
- keep browser attestation off the renderer while a dialog is open. ([#5524](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5524)) Thanks @abonneth.
- index disabled macOS controls and report enabled: false. ([#5635](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5635)) Thanks @kurtguenther; reported by @will-bogusz.
- remove stale screenshot tool references. ([#2317](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2317))
- return from a dom_event click when its handler opens a dialog. ([#5621](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5621)) Thanks @sahiljagtap08.
- clear clippy -D warnings on main. ([#6461](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6461))
- bind every sdk test socket under a short /tmp dir. ([#6466](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6466))
- force embedded mode in the SDK in-process loader tests. ([#6485](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6485))
- normalize list_windows z-index parity. ([#2172](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2172))
- detect Hyprland input internals instead of pinning 0.56.2. ([#6495](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6495)) Thanks @chrisohearn.
- refuse with 'did not verify' when cosign cannot start in install.ps1. ([#6483](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6483)) Thanks @sly321-pixel.
- add SPDX headers to cua-driver sources (CUA-3388). ([#6516](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6516))
- treat niri workspace read-backs the cleanup deadline cut off as unconfirmed. ([#6520](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6520))
- keep a full budget for each dom_event click readback. ([#6519](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6519))
- initialize recording hooks for embedded platform registries. ([#5785](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5785)) reported by @nick-inkeep.
- keep cua-driver-core clippy-clean without default features. ([#6543](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6543))
- raise own-process windows on the AppKit main queue (CUA-3309). ([#6559](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6559))
- return from a trusted browser click when its handler opens a dialog. ([#6562](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6562))
- Windows type_text posts UTF-16 units in order and repairs dropped tails (CUA-3122). ([#6341](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/6341))

## Performance

- build the tool contract manifest once per process. ([#5977](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5977)) Thanks @gakonst.

## Contributors

Thanks to @abonneth, @ayagmar, @BhaveshY, @chrisohearn, @CMGS, @cristicretu, @factory-ain3sh, @Faraclas, @gakonst, @Iflaqbhat, @jhugman, @Katechnology, @kurtguenther, @louistiti, @lucasfdale, @MankhongGarden, @nick-inkeep, @philipljh, @sahiljagtap08, @ShadyElsharnoby, @skap3214, @sly321-pixel, @smraikai, @stanley50z, @will-bogusz, @ymqy for contributing to this release.

## Install

macOS and Linux:

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"
```

Windows:

```powershell
irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex
```

Cua Driver ships universal macOS binaries, x86_64 and arm64 Windows builds,
and Linux preview builds. Release assets also include tag-pinned installer and
uninstaller scripts.

## Why GitHub says “Pre-release”

GitHub's label is used only to keep this monorepo's repository-wide “Latest”
pointer from switching between independently released products. A plain Cua
Driver SemVer is a stable release; npm and PyPI publish it on
their normal stable channels, and the installers resolve the versioned
`cua-driver-rs-v*` releases directly.
